persona.title: Pretend you are…
persona.text: Pretend you are Wanjiru, 20, a college student in Nakuru who also leads her church youth group. She is planning a youth football tournament and is also trying to find money for next term's school fees. Everything is in her head, and today she cannot remember what she was supposed to do next, or who she is waiting for.

lines: Welcome. This short video explains an app called Next Step Board. In about four minutes you will know what it is for and how to use it.
First, the problem. Most of us carry many projects at the same time. School work. A church event. Fees. A small business. A repair at home.
Big projects get stuck when the next move is not clear. You feel tired and do nothing. Or you forget that you were waiting for someone to answer you.
Next Step Board fixes this with one simple idea. For every project, write down only one thing: the next small step, and whose turn it is.
Who uses it? Students, youth leaders, church volunteers, small business owners. Anyone with many things going on at once.
Let us look at the screen, slowly.

lines.t: At the very top is the name of the board. It says My Next Step Board. Tap the name to change it, for example to Youth Group or Home.
Under the name is a row of buttons: All, Active, Waiting, Blocked, Paused, and Needs me. They choose which cards you see. All shows every card. Needs me shows only the cards where it is your turn.
Below that is a box called Where you left off. It counts your projects and tells you which one to start with today.

lines: Under the box are the cards. Each card is one project, with its name and, on the right, a small label: active, waiting, blocked or paused.

lines.t: The most important part of a card is the line called Next step. One small thing to do, and under it, who will do it and how long it takes.

Under the next step is a row of buttons. The pencil button called Next changes the next step. The button called Status, with a small arrow, changes the label. Tap it once and active becomes waiting. Tap again for blocked, then paused, then back to active.

lines: Waiting means the ball is in someone else's court. You did your part, and now you wait for an answer. Paused means you will come back to it later. Blocked means something is stopping you.
There is also a line with plus due date. Tap it and type a date. The app wants the American order: month first, then day, then year. So the 31st of October 2026 is typed as 10 slash 31 slash 2026.
At the bottom of each card is the Checklist. Tap it to open it. Type a small job in the box that says add an item, and tap Add. When a job is finished, tap the tick box next to it.
To add a new project, scroll to the bottom of the page and tap plus Add project. A form slides up. Type the project name, the next step, and who will do it. Then tap Add it.
Everything saves on this phone by itself. There is no account.

At the bottom you will also see a button called Start blank. It removes every card so you can begin with an empty board. And at the very bottom of the page is Start fresh, which erases everything this app saved.
Here is the habit. Every morning, read down the board and do the next steps that are yours.
In the test, you will be Wanjiru, a student and youth leader in Nakuru. Take your time. If something is confusing, say so. Confusing parts are exactly what we want to find.

challenge.intro: Now you are Wanjiru. The board will be empty. Nobody will tell you which button to press. Use what you learned. When you finish, tap Check my work.
challenge.start: Open Next Step Board with the normal app link (not the 🧪 test copy). If the welcome card shows, tap 'skip the tour' → '✨ Start fresh with my own' → OK, and the board is empty. If it does not show: scroll to the very bottom of the page and tap '🧹 Start fresh — erase this app’s data' → OK → OK (if it says there is nothing to erase, just tap OK). The example cards come back after the reload, so scroll down to the buttons at the bottom and tap 'Start blank' → OK. The board now says 'No projects yet'. (Verified 10 Oct: all five checks false after this.)

tasks.text: Give the board the name Youth Group.
tasks.hint: The board's name is the big title at the very top. Tap it.

tasks.text: Add a project for the youth football tournament. Its next step is to book the school field.
tasks.check: (function(){try{var d=JSON.parse(localStorage.getItem('nextstep_board_v1')||'null');if(!d||!d.projects)return false;var ps=d.projects;var low=function(s){return String(s==null?'':s).trim().toLowerCase()};var f=ps.filter(function(p){var n=low(p.name);return n.indexOf('football')>=0||n.indexOf('tournament')>=0});return f.some(function(p){return low(p.next).indexOf('field')>=0})}catch(e){return false}})()
tasks.hint: Use '+ Add project' at the bottom of the board. Put the next step in the box called 'The next step'. If the card already exists, use '✏️ Next' on it.

tasks.text: The tournament also needs three jobs: buy a ball, call six teams, find a referee. Put them on the tournament's list, and show that you have already bought the ball.
tasks.check: (function(){try{var d=JSON.parse(localStorage.getItem('nextstep_board_v1')||'null');if(!d||!d.projects)return false;var ps=d.projects;var low=function(s){return String(s==null?'':s).trim().toLowerCase()};var f=ps.filter(function(p){var n=low(p.name);return n.indexOf('football')>=0||n.indexOf('tournament')>=0});return f.some(function(p){var t=p.tasks||[];var has=function(w){return t.filter(function(x){return low(x[0]).indexOf(w)>=0})};var b=has('ball'),tm=has('team'),r=has('referee');return b.length&&tm.length&&r.length&&b.some(function(x){return !!x[2]})&&!tm.some(function(x){return !!x[2]})&&!r.some(function(x){return !!x[2]})})}catch(e){return false}})()
tasks.hint: Open the Checklist at the bottom of the tournament card. Add each job with the 'add an item…' box, then tick only the job that is already done.

tasks.text: Add a project for next term's school fees. You have already asked Uncle Otieno to help, and now you are waiting for his answer. Make the card show that.
tasks.hint: After you add the fees project, look at the small label on its card. The 'Status ▸' button changes it. Which word means you are waiting for someone else?

tasks.text: The school field must be booked by 31 October 2026. Give the tournament that due date.
tasks.check: (function(){try{var d=JSON.parse(localStorage.getItem('nextstep_board_v1')||'null');if(!d||!d.projects)return false;var ps=d.projects;var low=function(s){return String(s==null?'':s).trim().toLowerCase()};var f=ps.filter(function(p){var n=low(p.name);return n.indexOf('football')>=0||n.indexOf('tournament')>=0});return f.some(function(p){return p.due==='2026-10-31'})}catch(e){return false}})()
tasks.hint: Tap '+ due date' on the tournament card. The app wants the American order: month/day/year, like 10/31/2026.

ownWords.question: In your own words, what is this app for?
keyIdeas: shows every project on one screen
each project has one small next step and who does it
shows which projects are waiting on someone else, so nothing is forgotten

daily.task: Move one card to its next column in Next Step Board — or add one new card.
